Octopus intelligence in the deep sea

Octopuses are among the most intelligent invertebrates on Earth. A single octopus brain contains roughly 500 million neurons, two thirds of which are distributed through its eight arms.

In captivity, octopuses have been observed opening screw-top jars, solving mazes, and recognizing individual human faces.

Wild octopuses use tools such as coconut shells as portable shelters while they move across the seafloor.
